account:
Today has mostly been routine mayoral business, with an unresolved mill inspection and persistent but unsubstantiated talk about the river crossing. I read my appointments this morning, attended the mill at ten, returned home for lunch, dealt with council correspondence in the office, visited my neighbour for tea, and returned late for the sixteen-thirty office appointment. No new council letters or urgent decisions have been reported. I am now in the office shortly before eighteen; my neighbour has arrived for a possible walk, and I am due home at nineteen.

The unusual news is repeated talk of a 'bridge or port change at bakery.' Townsfolk have mentioned the baker, freight, innkeeper and neighbour as having been there, but I have not witnessed any such discussion or seen a proposal. My neighbour says they visited the bakery but personally heard no crossing discussion and noticed no urgent river concern. The secretary reports that the baker likewise witnessed no crossing change, heard only vague rumours, and knows of no assistance needed. Those accounts do not prove that no proposal exists, but I currently have no verified change, purpose, decision-maker or need for action. I should not treat repeated gossip as independent confirmation.

The mill inspection remains unfinished. I found no staff or delivery records there; the seventy-six hay bales I saw at its stall are not a full grain audit. The secretary also found no staff, and the responsible mill contact remains unidentified. The intended inspection concerns grain stocks, delivery records, shortages and storage conditions; it was not an instruction to move supplies. Someone reported the innkeeper carrying hay at the mill, but I do not know why, and that alone establishes no connection to the crossing rumour or any wrongdoing. I have asked the secretary to record the uncertainty and keep the mill follow-up pending for tomorrow's briefing.
